items.title: Randy Sandke interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997
items.q: to quote Jack Walrath, who was kind of like saying, he was like speaking against this idea of trying to form

ctx.x: Well you said it about five times already, that the music was the focus. That the music brought them together I would guess.

And I mean the thing that ultimately anything that divides, I mean that’s another irony is that the whole thing about jazz is that it was kind of melting pot. What keeps it alive is all the influences coming in. When you get into this like racial purification it’s kind of like Nazi talk. I mean that’s the opposite of art, the opposite of something living, breathing. It’s got to take in, to quote Jack Walrath, who was kind of like saying, he was like speaking against this idea of trying to form, saying that this…

Russia, they sent me a record, really good players. And I wrote back to them and I said this record is great but it sounds like it was made in New York. I said you know like there’s so many interesting rhythmic things in the music from your part of the world, put some of that in there.
